before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Wonderful. Which page explains that leftover door?

before.speaker: B
before.text: Could you hold it for a second?

before.speaker: A
before.text: Certainly. Just to clarify: you're asking for my help?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Right, I'll get this cupboard standing straight. Pass me the instructions and we'll sort it out.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I can read them. I only need someone to hold the door.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Excellent. You read; I'll manage the holding. Tell me where you want my hands.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Here, while I put the hinge in. Don't move until I say.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Perfect. I'll keep it steady under your direction. That means you do need me for this bit, doesn't it?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've brought a blanket. Your heater's still broken? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'm managing. Leave the blanket, though.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Gladly. Would you say you needed my help?

before.speaker: B
before.text: I need the blanket. I can reset the heater myself.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Of course. The fuse box is in my locked cupboard. Shall I wait while you manage?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've brought the blanket. We'll get you warm first, then I'll supervise the heater reset.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I know how to reset it. Could you just leave the blanket?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Of course. I'll take care of warmth, you take care of the switch. That's the sensible division.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Actually, could you hold the blanket round me while I reach behind the heater?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Certainly. You direct the reset; I'll keep this tucked in. Just say you need my hands here, and I won't move them.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before you get your train, could you taste this soup? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: It needs salt.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'll fix that. You'll need to check again.

before.speaker: B
before.text: My train leaves in ten minutes.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Perfect. That's when the bread comes out.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll get lunch right before your train. Taste this soup and I'll make the final adjustment.

after.speaker: B
after.text: It needs salt, but I haven't time for a whole bowl.

after.speaker: A
after.text: One spoonful will do. I'll season just that and you can give me the verdict.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I'll take it in a flask. I really must go.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Excellent plan. Hold the flask while I pour, then check one drop from the lid. I won't send you off with a lunch you haven't signed off on.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before you zip your suitcase, let me wrap that jar of jam. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: It's already wrapped in my jumper.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. That's your train jumper. We'll need to unpack it and find something else.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'll leave the jam here.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Then you haven't tasted it. I'll get a spoon before you decide.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll finish your packing. Give me the jam jar and I'll wrap it properly before you close the case.

after.speaker: B
after.text: It's already wrapped in my jumper. I need to leave.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Good thinking. I'll tuck the sleeves round the lid; just check the glass with me so we know it won't leak.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I'd rather leave the jar here than keep fussing with it.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Sensible. I'll look after it. Have one taste from a spoon before you decide it's mine to keep; you can tell me whether I should save you another jar.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've put your usual mug out. We can still have tea. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Still? Are you cross with me?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'm hoping you won't leave me cross.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Could you try one where you're sorry about yourself? I'll keep the tea warm.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've set out our mugs. We'll put this right over tea and have a pleasant afternoon.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Are you cross with me? I don't want another argument.

after.speaker: A
after.text: No argument. You can take your time; I'd just like to hear that you're sorry before I pour.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I'm sorry you're upset. Is that enough?

after.speaker: A
after.text: It's a start. I'll pour while you try the part about yourself. Just one sentence, and we can have the afternoon I promised.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Your parents arrive in ten minutes. I'd like to be able to smile at you. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I thought we'd sorted this out by text.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. You sent a thumbs-up. I couldn't hear any remorse.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'll send a sad face.

before.speaker: A
before.text: You're right here. Could you give the sad face a sentence beginning with 'I'?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Your parents arrive in ten minutes. I'll get us smiling before they ring; we only need to finish one small conversation.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I thought we'd finished it by text.

after.speaker: A
after.text: The thumbs-up was a useful start. Give me the words that go with it and I'll call us ready.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I can send a sad face if that helps.

after.speaker: A
after.text: It does. Keep the phone down and give me that face with a sentence starting 'I'm sorry.' Quietly is fine; I just need to hear it before I open the door.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Would you support a small improvement to the front garden? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: What sort of improvement?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Something with a pond. And no tree.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Where's the tree?

before.speaker: A
before.text: Let's finish agreeing before the stump grinder leaves.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've got the garden improvement under control. A little pond will make the front look lovely, if you're happy with it.

after.speaker: B
after.text: What about the tree? I like the shade.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've arranged a bench with a canopy. You can choose where it goes; I want your shady corner kept.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Why are you replacing the tree's shade? Where is it?

after.speaker: A
after.text: It's been cut down. I'll stop the grinder until you've chosen what happens next. If I keep that corner shaded exactly as you want, can we call the pond a good decision?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. How do you feel about me inviting a few people to dinner? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Tonight? We have two chairs.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. So standing guests would be more considerate?

before.speaker: B
before.text: How many people?

before.speaker: A
before.text: Six. I've already invited them. Would borrowing enough chairs for everyone turn that into a yes?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll manage dinner tonight. A few guests will be lovely, provided you're with me on it.

after.speaker: B
after.text: We only have two chairs. I don't want people standing round my plate.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then everyone gets a seat. I'll borrow the chairs and you can choose the table arrangement.

after.speaker: B
after.text: How many have you asked already?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Six. I've sent the invitations. I'll do the fetching and the washing-up as well; can you give me a yes on the dinner if the seating is yours to settle?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. These eighty wedding place cards need names. Your bin labels have better lettering than our invitations. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I like calligraphy. I hate copying guest lists.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'd read the names. You'd only do the beautiful part.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Your aunt will complain if I use purple.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'll handle my aunt. The ink colour could be entirely yours.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll have these eighty wedding cards finished tonight. Your lettering would make them worth keeping; would you take the pen?

after.speaker: B
after.text: I like lettering. I don't want to copy a guest list all evening.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Good. I'll read every name to you. You can make each card look exactly as you like.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Even purple? Your aunt will make you ask me to change it.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Purple is now my color scheme. I'll tell her that before she sees them. Will you start with her name while I read it out?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. You have such a good eye for storage. Sorting our shed could finally give your tools a proper home. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Until you dump paint tins everywhere again.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. You could assign every shelf. I'd follow your labels.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Including a shelf you're forbidden to touch?

before.speaker: A
before.text: Absolutely. You could put it at eye level so I see what I'm missing.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'm getting this shed organized. Your tools deserve proper shelves; would you like to decide where everything belongs?

after.speaker: B
after.text: Only until you dump paint tins wherever you like.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then I'll carry the tins and you assign their places. I'll follow the labels; that will be our system.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Including a shelf you're not allowed to touch?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Absolutely. I'll announce that rule myself. Pick the shelf you want protected, and I'll clear it first if you'll take on the rest.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. When you say you heard about the party, which part? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: The cake went over the balcony. Was that before you left?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Who gave you the timing?

before.speaker: B
before.text: Nobody. Your brother says there's a video.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Have you watched it, or are we both relying on my brother?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll straighten out this party story. Tell me exactly what you've heard before it gets any bigger.

after.speaker: B
after.text: The cake went over the balcony. But I'm not naming who told me.

after.speaker: A
after.text: No names needed. We can keep this informal. Did you hear a description, or actually see what happened?

after.speaker: B
after.text: There's supposed to be a video. I haven't watched it.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Good, we're working from the same report then. Keep your source to yourself; just tell me whether anyone has described what's visible in the video.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. What did the manager say about the missing keys? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: They might be in the drain. You locked up, didn't you?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Is she asking everyone who locked up, or just me?

before.speaker: B
before.text: Just you. Someone saw you outside.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Did they say what I was doing, or only where I was?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll handle the missing-key questions. What has the manager actually said so far?

after.speaker: B
after.text: She thinks they're in the drain. I'm not getting between you two.

after.speaker: A
after.text: You won't have to. Just help me separate what she knows from what she's asking. Has anyone said they saw the keys?

after.speaker: B
after.text: Only that someone saw you outside after closing.

after.speaker: A
after.text: That's useful. No need to speak for her; did they mention my hands, or only where I was standing? We'll keep it to what was actually seen.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Will you keep Mum in the kitchen while I hide her birthday cake? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Only if you stop telling her I'm the one who plans these things.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. This one's mine. Could you ask her to show you her pastry trick?

before.speaker: B
before.text: She'll make me bake a whole pie.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'll peel the apples tonight. Could you get us twenty minutes and a pie?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I've got Mum's surprise organized. You keep her in the kitchen while I hide the cake, and I'll give you the signal.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Only if you tell her this was your plan. I got blamed for the last surprise.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Of course. My plan, my responsibility. Ask her for the pastry lesson; I'll work round whatever time she gives you.

after.speaker: B
after.text: She'll make me bake an entire pie.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then I'll do the filling and wash up afterwards. You choose when to end the lesson, and I'll call that the signal. Can I count on you for the kitchen?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Will you help me set up Denise's surprise leaving party at seven? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I spent the last one washing glasses.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'll wash up. Could you get Denise out of the office while I decorate?

before.speaker: B
before.text: She won't leave before I finish her spreadsheet.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Send it over. I'll finish her spreadsheet; could you take her for coffee and complain about how little I do?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll run Denise's surprise party at seven. I need you to get her out of the office while I put the decorations up.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I spent your last party washing glasses. I'm not doing that again.

after.speaker: A
after.text: You won't. I'll wash them. Your job can be coffee with Denise, somewhere you actually like.

after.speaker: B
after.text: She won't leave until her spreadsheet is finished.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Send it to me. I'll finish it before I decorate; you choose the cafe and the time. Tell me when you're taking her, and I'll make my schedule fit.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Your rooftop wedding photo would look lovely. Try that staff-only door first. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'm the bride. They'll notice me.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. They'll forgive you. I'll follow once you've explained the dress.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Then carry my train.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Gladly. I'll hold the very end, so if they object, only your train has followed you in.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll get you the best wedding photograph. Try that staff-only door to the roof; I'll bring the camera behind you.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I'm the bride. Everyone will notice me going in.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then we'll make it look like the photograph is expected. You can explain the dress; I'll follow your lead at the door.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Only if you carry my train. I'm not doing this alone.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Of course. I'll take the end and keep it off the floor. You step through first so it doesn't catch, and I'll come when you've shown me there's room.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Try a grape before we buy the bunch. Last week's were sour. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: The sign says no tasting.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Just one. I'll try the next if nobody objects.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Fine, but you're holding the bunch where the assistant can see you.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Of course. I'll hold it out like samples. You take the first one; if that works, I'll serve myself.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll choose us a decent bunch this time. Taste that grape first; we won't buy sour ones again.

after.speaker: B
after.text: The sign says no tasting.

after.speaker: A
after.text: One will tell us enough. You try it and I'll take the next if the assistant is happy with that.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Then you hold the bunch where she can see it. No hiding behind me.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Certainly. I'll present it properly; you can make the first selection. Give me a nod if she lets you finish, and I'll join you.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before you cut the ribbon, whose bridge is this? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: The whole town's.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. And who stopped it leaning into the river?

before.speaker: B
before.text: You did. We thanked the engineers.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Lovely. Could one engineer have a name?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll give you the signal to cut the ribbon. First, introduce the engineer who kept this bridge out of the river.

after.speaker: B
after.text: This is the town's day. I don't want a speech about one person.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Quite right. One sentence will do, and then straight to the town. I'll keep the ceremony moving.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I've already thanked the engineering team.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then just add 'especially' and my name. That can finish the thanks you've given. Give me that much, and I'll signal the ribbon straight away.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. You've thanked the wedding guests. What about the person who cooked? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Everyone knows you made the food.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then why does the programme thank 'the buffet'?

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'll make an announcement.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Good. The buffet would like its surname pronounced correctly.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll keep dinner on schedule. Before dessert, please thank the person who cooked it all.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Everyone knows it was you. We can't stop for another speech.

after.speaker: A
after.text: No speech. One sentence while I bring the plates through will fit my schedule perfectly.

after.speaker: B
after.text: All right. I'll say the buffet was made by you. How do I pronounce your surname?

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll say it quietly for you first. Then use it once, clearly, while I set the dessert down. That will give me my cue as well as my credit.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Come to my birthday instead of the concert. I've made your favourite cake. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I've already bought tickets.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Bring your concert friend too. I'll reimburse both tickets in cake.

before.speaker: B
before.text: She only went because I promised her dancing.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'll clear the living room. You can choose the music; I'd just like to be in the room with you.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll give you a better birthday evening here than that concert. I've got your favorite cake and the whole night planned.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I've bought tickets, and I promised my friend we'd go together.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Bring her. I'll fit both of you into the plan; she can have the first slice if that helps.

after.speaker: B
after.text: She wanted dancing, not sitting round a cake.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then I'll clear the living room and put the cake aside. You two choose the music. I can host exactly that sort of evening, if you'll choose to have it with me.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Take me as your expedition photographer instead of Martin. I speak French. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: We're crossing a desert, not interviewing people.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Your sponsor's French. I could send them updates they can actually use.

before.speaker: B
before.text: They want their logo visible in every picture.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'll put it on the water flask. Martin photographs untouched wilderness; I'll make sure yours looks generously funded.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Choose me over Martin for the expedition photographs. I'll manage the pictures and send your French sponsor reports they can use.

after.speaker: B
after.text: We need desert pictures, not a polished report about them.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then pictures first. You can set the shot list; I'll make the reports fit what you actually need to show.

after.speaker: B
after.text: The sponsor wants its logo visible in every picture.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Put it on the water flask and I'll frame it where you want. Martin likes untouched wilderness; I can give you the desert your sponsor paid to see. You approve the first frame before I take the rest.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Sam's is sharper.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll settle the reunion poster today. Which photo would you put first, mine or Sam's?

after.speaker: B
after.text: Sam's. It's sharper.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Sharpness first, then. We'll keep that standard. You can send both to the committee; just put mine at the top so they see the choice.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I'll give them the same size and put them side by side.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Very fair of you. After all those weekends I spent helping you move. Side by side is fine; could mine be on the left? I'll call that the reading order.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Could you keep Friday free? I might need help moving. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I've promised to help Alex paint.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Right. Paint takes priority. Could you at least leave your phone on?

before.speaker: B
before.text: Of course. Have you actually found a flat?

before.speaker: A
before.text: Still looking. Nice that I'm worth a charged battery. This is just planning.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll have the move organized before Friday. Can I put you down as my first call for carrying boxes?

after.speaker: B
after.text: I've already promised Alex I'd help paint.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Alex first. Good to know where the day stands. I'll keep the heavy work flexible if you leave your phone on.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Of course. But have you actually found a flat yet?

after.speaker: A
after.text: Still choosing. A charged phone is a useful start; I'll put you under available rather than confirmed. Nothing personal, just keeping the plan tidy.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Let me have the medal for the charity auction. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then it should raise more than the toaster.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll make your medal the star of the charity auction, if you'll let me put it up for sale.

after.speaker: B
after.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then your name goes beside it, with the story of the race. You can choose every word; I'll make sure nobody mistakes it for just another lot.

after.speaker: B
after.text: Could I lend it for the display? I want people to know I won, but I want it back.

after.speaker: A
after.text: You can open the display yourself. Then, if you're willing, present it to the buyer. I'll keep your name in the programme after it's gone; would that let you part with it?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Would you sell your signed guitar so we can replace the fridge? Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I queued all night for that signature.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then let's price it properly. Those hours should buy us an ice maker.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Keep the case. You can still tell the queue story while I photograph the guitar.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll get us a proper price for your signed guitar. Would you let me sell it so we can replace the fridge?

after.speaker: B
after.text: I queued all night for that signature.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Then we won't treat it like a second-hand instrument. You can write the history for the advert, and I'll make the price reflect it.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

after.speaker: A
after.text: Keep the case for the memory. Let me bring you an offer for the guitar before you decide; you can refuse any amount. I'll handle the selling, but I need you to choose the price you could live with.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've started investigating the broken vase. First, we check the window. Please.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

before.speaker: A
before.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Excellent clue. I'll inspect the glue cupboard personally.

before.speaker: B
before.text: A piece of vase is stuck to you.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Good. Put me in charge of preserving it.

after.speaker: A
after.text: I'll organize the vase investigation. Let's start with that open window; you can tell me which way the wind was blowing.

after.speaker: B
after.text: I saw your elbow knock it off the table.
